whatItIs.text: Immature pods of the common bean, harvested before the seeds inside fill out — eaten pod and all, unlike dried beans.

historyNote.text: The common bean was cultivated in Mexico and Peru for thousands of years; the stringless bean that modern shoppers expect was only bred in 1894 by Calvin Keeney, the 'father of the stringless bean', in New York.

howToChoose.text: Choose pods that snap cleanly and feel firm, with no limpness or brown spots; smaller beans are usually more tender.

storage.text: Refrigerate loosely bagged in the crisper and do not wash until use. The rulebook has the window.

foodSafetyRef.note: storage windows live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Even tired beans shine blanched then flash-fried with garlic, or in a slow braise with tomato; older pods can be stringed with a paring knife.

substitutions.note: sweeter, cook in half the time
add straight to the pan; softer texture
